title: annotations/<source>.jsonl
description: Expert teacher annotations of tutoring transcripts. There is one file per provider, and every provider is on this one schema. A row is one moment (a stretch of transcript an annotator selected as a teaching decision point) with every annotator's entry on it, or one annotator's record that a transcript had no such moment (`moment` is null). Each moment passed through three roles: a selector picked it and annotated it, a reannotator annotated it independently and may move its boundaries or throw it out, and one or two adjudicators settled the final answer. Annotators appear as stable labels (`A01` and so on), one per person across providers. The instructions the annotators followed are in `docs/annotation_guide.md`.

transcript_id.description: UUIDv5 surrogate for the annotated transcript. Joins to `transcripts/<source>.jsonl` `transcript_id`.

source.description: The provider the transcript came from; matches the file name.

purpose.description: What the annotation was for. `rigor_scaffolding`: selecting the moments where the tutor had to choose between scaffolding and pushing for rigor, and judging the tutor's choice.

batch.description: The annotation campaign this row came from.

moment.description: The selected moment, as the selector drew it. Null on a row recording that the transcript had no key moments.

v1_rigor_hinted.description: Whether the annotation tool showed annotators where the earlier v1 annotations had marked rigor on this transcript. True on some provider A transcripts only. Researchers can use it to account for annotators being steered towards those regions.

v1_rigor_regions.description: The turn ranges shown as v1 rigor hints, each as [first turn, last turn]. Empty unless `v1_rigor_hinted`.

annotations.description: Every annotator's entry on the moment, in the order the tool recorded them. Where an annotator saved the same role more than once, only their last save is kept. A row with no moment has exactly one entry.

AnnotatorLabel.description: The annotator's ID. One label per person, the same in every provider's file.

moment_id.description: UUIDv5 surrogate for the moment. Unique within the file; benchmark rows refer to moments by it.

start_turn.description: First turn of the moment: the start of the situation that leads to the tutor's decision.

cut_turn.description: The last turn before the tutor's decision. The benchmark gives a model the transcript up to and including this turn.

end_turn.description: Last turn of the moment. A moment ends after the tutor's first strategy decision following the cut and the student's response to it.

status.description: `adjudicated`: the moment went through every role and has a final answer. `thrown_out`: a later role ruled the selection unusable (see the entries' `meta.throw_out_reason`).

selected_by.description: The annotator who selected the moment.

in_v1_rigor_region.description: Whether the moment overlaps a v1 rigor hint. Null where the transcript had no hints.

role.description: The annotator's role on this moment. Sets the shape of `payload`.

interface_version.description: Version of the annotation tool the entry was saved in.

schema_version.description: Version of the tool's answer format. The payload fields are the same across these versions.

enrichment_numbers.description: Provider A only: the transcript's `enrichments` (screen events narrated from the video) that fall inside the stretch this entry annotated, by `enrichment_number`.

payload.description: The annotator's answers. Its shape depends on `role`, or is a no-key-moments record when the row has no moment.

Situation.description: What strategy the moment called for, judged from the transcript up to the cut. Both can be true.

scaffolding_appropriate.description: Scaffolding the student would be an appropriate move here.

rigor_appropriate.description: Pushing the student for rigor would be an appropriate move here.

Action.description: The tutor's first strategy decision after the cut, up to the end of the moment. The tutor may have scaffolded, pushed for rigor, both, or neither.

scaffolding_present.description: The tutor scaffolded: gave support that makes the task more accessible to the student.

scaffolding_amount.description: Whether the amount of scaffolding was right. `over_scaffolding`: too much support, replacing the student's thinking. `under_scaffolding`: too little. `appropriate`: the right level, even if aimed at the wrong difficulty (the annotator then says so in `explanation`). `unclear`: hard to tell. Null when `scaffolding_present` is false.

scaffolding_strategies.description: Scaffolding strategies the tutor used. `guiding_questions`: questions leading the student towards the solution. `break_into_steps`: breaks the problem into steps. `re_explain`: re-explains a concept (different example, metaphor or phrasing). `re_explain_procedure`: re-explains a procedure (likewise). `model_example`: models an example solution. `co_solve`: solves some steps for the student. `simpler_language`: rephrases the problem more simply, or gives a simpler alternative. `draw_diagram`: draws a diagram. `different_representation`: represents the problem differently (another form, a real-world analogy). `reduce_options`: narrows the answer options. `hint`: gives a starting point. `remind_prior_problem`: points back to a similar earlier problem. `highlight_problem_text`: highlights parts of the problem text. `give_answer`: gives away the answer. `state_correction`: states a correction.

scaffolding_strategy_other.description: Free-text strategy not in the list; empty when none.

over_scaffolding_reasons.description: How the tutor over-scaffolded. Empty unless `scaffolding_amount` is `over_scaffolding`. Each means the tutor unnecessarily: `most_cognitive_work` did most of the cognitive work; `no_opening_contribute` gave no opening for the student to contribute; `no_opening_demonstrate` gave no opening for the student to show what they can do; `procedural_insufficient_reasoning` reduced the task to procedural steps with too little reasoning; `premature_scaffolding` scaffolded before the student had shown what they can do; `gives_away_answers` gave away answers or key steps; `over_explains` over-explained; `re_scaffolds` scaffolded the same procedure or concept too many times; `oversimplifies` oversimplified the problem; `fails_to_fade` failed to fade the scaffolding; `jumps_in_struggle` jumped in during productive struggle.

rigor_present.description: The tutor pushed for rigor: raised the conceptual challenge to build critical thinking, independence and deeper understanding.

rigor_amount.description: How strong the push for rigor was. `strong`: the student is expected to demonstrate and communicate deep knowledge, e.g. explain why something works or find their own mistakes. `weak`: the tutor seems to intend a push but falls short, e.g. a question answerable by guessing, recall or following leading prompts. `unclear`: hard to tell, or in between. Null when `rigor_present` is false.

rigor_strategies.description: Rigor strategies the tutor used. `justify_explain`: asks the student to justify or explain an answer, solution or process. `withdraw_support`: lets the student work independently or struggle productively. `increase_complexity`: raises the problem's complexity or difficulty. `define_term`: asks the student to define or use a key mathematical term. `find_fix_errors`: asks the student to find and fix their own errors.

rigor_strategy_other.description: Free-text strategy not in the list; empty when none.

Result.description: How the student responded to the tutor's decision, judged within the moment.

problem_success.description: The student's success on the problem within the moment.

cognitive_engagement.description: The student's cognitive engagement within the moment.

other_observations.description: Anything else the annotator noted; empty when nothing.

ReannotatorMeta.description: The reannotator's ruling on the selection itself.

throw_out.description: The reannotator ruled the selection unusable. Their situation, action and result are then null.

changed_boundaries.description: The reannotator moved the moment's start or end.

redrew_cut_point.description: The reannotator moved the cut. Ground-truth builds drop these moments, since the annotators then judged different excerpts.

other_observations.description: Anything else the annotator noted; empty when nothing.

Decision.description: Where the adjudicator's answer for this section came from: `agreed` (the two annotators already agreed), `selector` or `reannotator` (took that annotator's answer), `combined` (wrote their own from both).

final.description: Null when the adjudicator threw the moment out.

decisions.description: Per section, where the final answer came from. Null when the adjudicator threw the moment out.

final_start_turn.description: The moment's start as adjudicated; null when thrown out.

final_cut_turn.description: The cut as adjudicated; null when thrown out.

final_end_turn.description: The moment's end as adjudicated; null when thrown out.

reverted_throw_out.description: The reannotator had thrown the moment out and the adjudicator reinstated it.

throw_out.description: The adjudicator ruled the selection unusable.

throw_out_category.description: Why, as a category; null unless `throw_out`.

throw_out_reason.description: Why, in the adjudicator's words; empty unless `throw_out`.

no_key_moments.description: The annotator found no key moment in the transcript.
